page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance designed to handle memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by the KVM hypervisor, this virtual machine runs on the x86_64 architecture and provides 24 dedicated vCPUs driven by 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processors. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a balanced 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no graphics processing units, centering its resource profile entirely on central processing and high memory capacity.

Network connectivity for the ecs.r6.6xlarge is provisioned with an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance features no integrated local storage and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring the configuration of external network-attached block storage and VPC routing for persistent data and external traffic. Because local disk storage is absent, data persistence and disk throughput rely on remote block storage performance, which represents a primary architectural consideration for I/O-intensive pipelines.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio allows organizations running memory-bound tasks to satisfy substantial footprint requirements without overpaying for idle compute cycles. This resource ratio prevents over-provisioning core counts merely to acquire necessary memory volumes. The ecs.r6.6xlarge is suited for in-memory databases such as Redis and Memcached, large relational databases, in-memory data analytics engines, enterprise resource planning backends, and intensive memory-cached data processing applications.
description: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for high-density enterprise computing workloads. Driven by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 24 dedicated vCPUs from the 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor family alongside 192.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a generous 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no dedicated local instance storage and no integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached block storage architectures alongside an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface. In terms of cost efficiency, the dense allocation of RAM per core allows organizations running memory-bound tasks to maximize compute resources without provisioning excessive CPU cores. The absence of built-in storage requires planning for remote disk I/O latency, making the instance an effective choice for memory-resident databases, distributed in-memory caches, enterprise resource planning systems, large-scale data analytics, and high-throughput real-time stream processing pipelines.
